SCCH-23 3 MVC. No.1240/2021  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 18.09.2020 at about 8.00 p.m.,
when Sri. G.A. Mohammed Munshid (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL24S0150 near Veerasandra Junction situated on Hosur Main road, Electronic City, Bengaluru, at that time a lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594 which was being driven by its driver in a rash & negligent manner came and dashed against the aforementioned motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the same on the spot itself.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
As the accident was caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594, the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Inspite of due service of notice of the petition upon him, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured lorry is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL24S0150 who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was responsible for the occurrence of the unfortunate accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that at the time of accident the insured lorry did not have permit & fitness certificate to ply in a public place and the driver thereof did not possess valid & effective driving licence.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to ) Sri. Mohammed Musthafa.

2 indemnify him.
Noncompliance of Sec's 134(c) & 158 (6) of the MV Act, 1988 is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased 'G.A. Mohammed Munshid' and were dependent on him ?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.09.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., near Veerasandra Junction situated on Hosur Main road, Electronic City,
Bengaluru, due to the actionable negligence of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594 ?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4.
What order or award?
5. The petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 19 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence on its behalf.
6. Oral arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.2 :

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri.Suraj Kumar.R, the Electronic City Police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594 for the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and 134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594 and as such issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.

3 8.
ISSUES NO.1 & 3
: These issues are taken up together for common consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts.

9. The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination and deposed that he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioners No.3 to 5 are the younger siblings of the deceased.
The documents placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
However no evidence has been adduced to show that the petitioners No.3 to 5 were financially dependent on the deceased.
Therefore in the absence of evidence I hold the claimants No.3 to 5 to be nondependents.

Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
10.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS : In the Aadhaar card (Ex.P13) the date of birth of deceased is reflected as 18.08.1995.
This indicates that he was aged 25 years at the time of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
11.
According to PW.1, the deceased was not only pursuing his Engineering degree but he was also working in a private firm and thereby earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ p.m.
However the income of the deceased is not substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident and age of the deceased, if his income is assessed at Rs.11,000/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others), the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 25 years.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
40% of Rs.11,000/ works out to Rs.4400/.
Therefore
the total income comes to Rs.15,400/ (11,000 + 4,400).

The deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.

1/2 of Rs.15,400/
works out to Rs.7,700/.
Income for consideration is Rs.7,700/ (15,400 - 7,700).
Annual income works out to Rs.92,400/ (7,700 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '18'.

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.16,63,200/ (92,400 X 18) which is rounded off to Rs.16,64,000/.
12.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM :
In addition to a sum of Rs.16,64,000/ towards Loss of dependency the petitioners No.1 & 2 are also entitled to Rs.40,000/ each towards filial consortium.
13. LOSS OF ESTATE: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
14. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

15. The calculation table stands as follows :

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
17. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the first respondent.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN48AU5594 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No's.1 & 3 are answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
18. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,74,000/ (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Seventy Four thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1  Rs.8,72,000/
 Petitioner No.2  Rs.8,72,000/
 Petitioner No.3  Rs.10,000/
 Petitioner No.4  Rs.10,000/
 Petitioner No.5  Rs.10,000/
Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% each shall be released to them through E payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
